questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: The v-x graph of a particle moving along x-axis is as shown in the figure. Then acceleration of the particle at x = 8 m is:
questionReview.mistakeHint: The numerical approach is likely correct but the unit or scale used in the final step is off. Verify unit conversions and dimensional consistency.
questionReview.explanation: Acceleration a = v (dv/dx). From the graph, slope dv/dx = -8/16 = -1/2. At x = 8 m, v = 8 -(1/2)(8) = 4 m/s. Therefore, a = 4 * (-1/2) = -2 m/s².

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: The graph shown in figure shows the velocity v versus time t for a body. Which of the graphs represents the corresponding acceleration versus time graphs?
questionReview.mistakeHint: The numerical approach is likely correct but the unit or scale used in the final step is off. Verify unit conversions and dimensional consistency.
questionReview.explanation: The slope of the v-t graph is negative and constant for the first half, and positive and constant over the second half. Therefore, acceleration is a negative constant followed by a positive constant, corresponding to graph (B).

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A ball is thrown vertically upwards. Which of the following graphs represents the velocity-time graph of the ball during its flight? (air resistance is neglected)
questionReview.mistakeHint: The wrong formula or relationship was applied here. Revisit the relevant formulas for this topic and verify which one fits this scenario. Topic: Vertical Motion Under Gravity.
questionReview.explanation: v = u - gt. The velocity-time relation is a straight line with a constant negative slope (-g), crossing the time axis when v = 0 at the highest point and continuing downwards, corresponding to graph (D).

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: If the displacement of a particle is x = 2t² + t + 5 meters, what will be its acceleration at t = 5 seconds?
questionReview.explanation: v = dx/dt = 4t + 1 m/s. a = dv/dt = 4 m/s². The acceleration is 4 m/s² at all times.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A man throws balls with the same speed vertically upwards, one after the other at an interval of 2 seconds. What should be the speed of the throw so that more than two balls are in the sky at any time? (Given g = 9.8 m/s²)
questionReview.explanation: For more than 2 balls to remain in the sky, the time of flight T of each ball must exceed 4 seconds (2 × 2 s). T = 2u/g > 4 => u > 2g = 2 × 9.8 = 19.6 m/s.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A particle starts from rest. Its acceleration (a) versus time (t) graph is as shown in the figure. The maximum speed of the particle will be:
questionReview.explanation: v_max - v_initial = Area under a-t graph = 1/2 × base × height = 1/2 × 11 × 10 = 55 m/s. Since u = 0, v_max = 55 m/s.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A body travels for 15 seconds starting from rest with constant acceleration. If it travels distances S₁, S₂, and S₃ in the first five seconds, second five seconds, and next five seconds respectively, the relation between S₁, S₂, and S₃ is:
questionReview.mistakeHint: The wrong formula or relationship was applied here. Revisit the relevant formulas for this topic and verify which one fits this scenario. Topic: Consecutive Time Distances.
questionReview.explanation: For motion from rest under constant acceleration, distances travelled in consecutive equal time intervals are in the ratio of odd numbers: S₁ : S₂ : S₃ = 1 : 3 : 5, hence S₁ = S₂ / 3 = S₃ / 5.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A particle is moving in a straight line with initial velocity u and uniform acceleration a. If the sum of the distance travelled in t-th and (t + 1)-th seconds is 100 cm, then its velocity after t seconds, in cm/s, is:
questionReview.explanation: S_t + S_(t+1) = [u + a(t - 1/2)] + [u + a(t + 1/2)] = 2(u + at) = 100 cm. Therefore, velocity after t seconds is v = u + at = 50 cm/s.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A metro train starts from rest and in five seconds achieves a speed 108 km/h. After that it moves with constant velocity and comes to rest after travelling 45 m with uniform retardation. If total distance travelled is 395 m, find total time of travelling.
questionReview.mistakeHint: This topic needs more study time. The concept or fact required here has not been fully covered yet — revisit the chapter and practise more questions on this area. Focus specifically on: Multi-stage Motion.
questionReview.explanation: Top speed v = 108 km/h = 30 m/s. Accelerating: t₁ = 5 s, s₁ = 1/2 × 30 × 5 = 75 m. Decelerating: s₃ = 45 m, t₃ = 2 × 45 / 30 = 3 s. Constant velocity: s₂ = 395 - (75 + 45) = 275 m => t₂ = 275 / 30 = 9.17 s. Total time = 5 + 9.17 + 3 = 17.17 s ≈17.2 s.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A particle moves along a straight line OX. At a time t (in seconds) the distance x (in metres) of the particle from O is given by x = 40 + 12t - t³. Value of x for the particle when it comes to rest momentarily is:
questionReview.mistakeHint: The wrong formula or relationship was applied here. Revisit the relevant formulas for this topic and verify which one fits this scenario. Topic: Instantaneous Rest.
questionReview.explanation: v = dx/dt = 12 - 3t². Setting v = 0 gives t² = 4 => t = 2 s. Position at t = 2 s: x = 40 + 12(2) -2³ = 40 + 24 - 8 = 56 m.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A body moving with a uniform acceleration crosses a distance of 65 m in the 5th second and 105 m in 9th second. How far will it go in 20 s?
questionReview.explanation: S_n = u + a(n - 1/2). S₅ = u + 4.5 a = 65. S₉ = u + 8.5 a = 105. Subtracting gives 4a = 40 => a = 10 m/s². Then u = 20 m/s. Total distance in 20 s: s = ut + 1/2 a t² = 20(20) + 1/2 (10) (20)² = 400 + 2000 = 2400 m.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A car, starting from rest, accelerates at the rate f through a distance S, then continues at constant speed for time t and then decelerates at the rate f / 2 to come to rest. If the total distance traversed is 15 S, then:
questionReview.mistakeHint: The numerical approach is likely correct but the unit or scale used in the final step is off. Verify unit conversions and dimensional consistency.
questionReview.explanation: Phase 1: S₁ = S = v² / (2f). Phase 3: S₃ = v² / (2 × f/2) = v² / f = 2S. Phase 2: S₂ = 15S - S - 2S = 12S. Also S₂ = v t => v = 12 S / t. Substituting into S = v² / (2f) gives S = (144 S² / t²) / (2f) => 1 = 72 S / (f t²) => S = (1/72) f t².

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A block of mass M is pulled along a horizontal frictionless surface by a rope of mass m. If a force P is applied at the free end of the rope, the force exerted by the rope on the block will be:
questionReview.mistakeHint: The numerical approach is likely correct but the unit or scale used in the final step is off. Verify unit conversions and dimensional consistency.
questionReview.explanation: Acceleration of the block + rope system: a = P / (M + m). The rope is the only horizontal force on the block, so the force exerted by the rope on the block = M a = M P / (M + m).

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: Two blocks of mass m = 1 kg and M = 2 kg are in contact on a frictionless table. A horizontal force F (= 3 N) is applied to m. The force of contact between the blocks will be:
questionReview.mistakeHint: Your approach looks right but a computational slip derailed the answer. Double-check each arithmetic step and watch for sign/factor errors. Topic: Contact Forces.
questionReview.explanation: Common acceleration a = F / (m + M) = 3 / (1 + 2) = 1 m/s². The contact force between the blocks accelerates block M: N = M × a = 2 × 1 = 2 N.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A stone thrown upward with a speed u from the top of a tower reaches the ground with a velocity 3u. The height of the tower is:
questionReview.mistakeHint: The wrong formula or relationship was applied here. Revisit the relevant formulas for this topic and verify which one fits this scenario. Topic: Motion Under Gravity.
questionReview.explanation: By conservation of energy / kinematics: v² = u² + 2gh ⇒(3u)² = u² + 2gh ⇒8u² = 2gh ⇒h = 4 u² / g.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: The pulley arrangements of fig. (a) and (b) are identical. The mass of the rope is negligible. In (a) the mass m is lifted up by attaching a mass 2m to the other end of the rope. In (b) m is lifted up by pulling the other end of the rope with a constant downward force F = 2mg. Which of the following is correct?
questionReview.explanation: In case (a): a₁ = (2m - m)g / (2m + m) = g/3. In case (b): a₂ = (F - mg) / m = (2mg - mg) / m = g. Therefore, a₂ = 3 a₁.

options.text: Acceleration in case (b) is 3 times more than that in case (a)
In case (a) acceleration is g, while in case (b) is 2g
In both cases, acceleration is the same

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A block of mass m is in contact with the cart C as shown in the figure. The coefficient of static friction between the block and the cart is μ. The acceleration α of the cart that will prevent the block from falling satisfies:
questionReview.explanation: In the accelerating frame of the cart, the block experiences a pseudo-force mα pressing it against the vertical cart face, giving a normal reaction N = mα and maximum upward static friction f_max = μN = μmα. To prevent the block from falling, μmα ≥mg ⇒α ≥g/μ.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A monkey is descending from the branch of a tree with constant acceleration. If the breaking strength of the branch is 75% of the weight of the monkey, the maximum acceleration with which monkey can slide down without breaking the branch is:
questionReview.mistakeHint: Your approach looks right but a computational slip derailed the answer. Double-check each arithmetic step and watch for sign/factor errors. Topic: Tension and Breaking Strength.
questionReview.explanation: While sliding down with acceleration a, the branch tension is T = m(g −a). The branch survives only if T ≤0.75 mg ⇒m(g −a) ≤0.75 mg ⇒a ≥g/4. So the limiting (critical) acceleration at which the branch is just about to break is a = g/4; the monkey must slide down with at least this acceleration.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: For the given situation as shown in the figure, the value of θ to keep the system in equilibrium will be:
questionReview.explanation: At the junction, T₂ = W = 60 N acts vertically downward and a 60 N force acts horizontally. T₁ makes angle θ with the vertical. Vertical balance: T₁ cos θ = 60 N. Horizontal balance: T₁ sin θ = 60 N. Dividing, tan θ = 1, so θ = 45°.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: Three equal weights of mass m each are hanging on a string passing over a fixed pulley as shown in the figure. The tensions in the string connecting weights A to B and B to C will respectively be:
questionReview.explanation: Mass on left side is m, mass on right side is 2m. System acceleration a = (2m - m)g / (3m) = g/3. For mass A: T_AB - mg = m(g/3) => T_AB = (4/3)mg. For bottom mass C: mg - T_BC = m(g/3) => T_BC = (2/3)mg. Thus tensions are (4/3)mg and (2/3)mg.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A train 120 m long travelling at 30 m/s starts overtaking another train 150 m long travelling at 15 m/s in the same direction. The time taken by the first train to pass the second train completely is:
questionReview.explanation: Relative distance to cover = 120 + 150 = 270 m. Relative speed = 30 −15 = 15 m/s. Time taken t = 270 / 15 = 18 s.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: Two automobiles are 150 kilometers apart and traveling towards each other. One automobile is moving at 60 km/h and the other is moving at 40 km/h. In how many hours will they meet?
questionReview.explanation: For motion towards each other, closing speed v_rel = 60 + 40 = 100 km/h. Time taken t = 150 / 100 = 1.5 h.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: The coordinate of a particle in meters is given by x(t) = 16t - 3.0 t³, where the time t is in seconds. The particle is momentarily at rest at t =
questionReview.mistakeHint: The wrong formula or relationship was applied here. Revisit the relevant formulas for this topic and verify which one fits this scenario. Topic: Variable Acceleration.
questionReview.explanation: Momentarily at rest ⇒v = dx/dt = 16 −9t² = 0 ⇒t² = 16/9 ⇒t = 4/3 s ≈1.33 s.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A force of 100 N acts in the direction as shown in the figure on a block of mass 10 kg resting on a smooth horizontal table. The speed acquired by the block after it has moved a distance of 10 m, will be: (in m/s) (take g = 10 m/s²)
questionReview.explanation: Horizontal component of force F_x = 100 cos 60° = 50 N. Acceleration a = F_x / m = 50 / 10 = 5 m/s². Using v² = u² + 2as with u = 0 and s = 10 m: v = √(2 × 5 × 10) = √100 = 10 m/s.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A thief is running away on a straight road in a jeep moving with a speed of 9 m/s. A policeman chases him on a motorcycle moving at a speed of 10 m/s. If the instantaneous separation of the jeep from the motorcycle is 100 m, how long will it take for the policeman to catch the thief?
questionReview.explanation: Relative speed along the same straight road v_rel = 10 −9 = 1 m/s. Time taken t = 100 / 1 = 100 s.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: Cathode rays are deflected away from a negatively charged plate because:
questionReview.mistakeHint: Your approach looks right but a computational slip derailed the answer. Double-check each arithmetic step and watch for sign/factor errors. Topic: Discovery of Subatomic Particles.
questionReview.explanation: Cathode rays consist of negatively charged electrons, which are repelled by a negatively charged plate.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: The energies of the 3s, 3p and 3d orbitals in a multielectron atom increase in that order. To which factor(s) can this order be attributed? I. the relative penetrations of these orbitals near the nucleus II. the relative average distance of the electron from the nucleus
questionReview.mistakeHint: This topic needs more study time. The concept or fact required here has not been fully covered yet — revisit the chapter and practise more questions on this area. Focus specifically on: Orbital Energies and Penetration.
questionReview.explanation: In a multi-electron atom the orbital energies for the same shell increase as E(3s) < E(3p) < E(3d). (I) Penetration: the s orbital penetrates closest to the nucleus, p less, d least, giving a larger effective nuclear charge and lower energy. (II) Average distance: the mean distance of the electron from the nucleus grows in the order 3s < 3p < 3d, so electron-nucleus attraction weakens in the same order. Both factors I and II are responsible.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: Which gas-phase atom in its ground state could have an electron with the quantum numbers n = 3, l = 2, m_l = 0, m_s = −1/2? (Given atomic numbers: Na = 11, Mg = 12, P = 15, Ti = 22)
questionReview.explanation: The quantum numbers n = 3, l = 2 specify a 3d orbital. Titanium (Z = 22) has ground-state configuration [Ar] 4s² 3d², which contains 3d electrons.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: Which orbital possesses one angular node and one radial node?
questionReview.explanation: Angular nodes = l = 1 (p-orbital). Radial nodes = n - l - 1 = 1 => n - 1 - 1 = 1 => n = 3. Thus, the 3p orbital has 1 angular node and 1 radial node.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: The first ionization energy of Na is 495.9 kJ/mol. What is the longest wavelength of light that could remove an electron from a Na atom?
questionReview.mistakeHint: This topic needs more study time. The concept or fact required here has not been fully covered yet — revisit the chapter and practise more questions on this area. Focus specifically on: Photoelectric Effect and Ionization.
questionReview.explanation: Ionization energy per atom E = (495.9 × 10³ J/mol) / (6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹) = 8.235 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. Maximum wavelength λ = hc / E = (6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ × 3 × 10⁸) / (8.235 × 10⁻¹⁹) = 2.41 × 10⁻⁷ m.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: What is the ratio of frequencies between the first lines of Lyman, Balmer and Paschen series?
questionReview.explanation: ν = R c (1/n₁² - 1/n₂²). Lyman first line (2 -> 1): 1 - 1/4 = 3/4. Balmer first line (3 -> 2): 1/4 - 1/9 = 5/36. Paschen first line (4 -> 3): 1/9 - 1/16 = 7/144. Ratio = 3/4 : 5/36 : 7/144.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: Which set of orbitals is listed in the sequential order of filling in a many-electron atom?
questionReview.explanation: According to the (n + l) rule: 3d (n+l = 5, n=3) -> 4p (n+l = 5, n=4) -> 5s (n+l = 5, n=5). Therefore, 3d, 4p, 5s is in direct sequential order.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: What is the electron configuration for a gas phase Fe³⁺ ion (Z = 26)?
questionReview.mistakeHint: Your approach looks right but a computational slip derailed the answer. Double-check each arithmetic step and watch for sign/factor errors. Topic: Transition Metal Electronic Configuration.
questionReview.explanation: Neutral Fe: [Ar] 4s² 3d⁶. Ionization removes the outer 4s electrons first, then 3d: losing three electrons yields [Ar] 3d⁵.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: Wavelength of a particular transition for H atom is 400 nm. What can be the wavelength of He⁺ for the same transition?
questionReview.explanation: 1/λ = R Z² (1/n₁² - 1/n₂²). For He⁺, Z = 2, so 1/λ_He = 4 (1/λ_H) => λ_He = λ_H / 4 = 400 nm / 4 = 100 nm.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: The correct sequence of frequency of electromagnetic radiations in electromagnetic spectrum is:
questionReview.mistakeHint: Your approach looks right but a computational slip derailed the answer. Double-check each arithmetic step and watch for sign/factor errors. Topic: Electromagnetic Spectrum.
questionReview.explanation: Frequency order is: X-rays (~10¹⁸ Hz) > UV rays (~10¹⁵ Hz) > Microwaves (~10¹⁰ Hz) > Radio waves (~10⁶ Hz).

options.text: X-rays > UV rays > Microwaves > Radio waves
Radio waves > Microwaves > UV rays > X-rays
UV rays > X-rays > Radio waves > Microwaves
Radio waves > Microwaves > X-rays > UV rays

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: The work function for a metal is 4 eV. To emit a photoelectron of zero velocity from the surface of the metal, the wavelength of incident light should be: [Given: h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s, c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s]
questionReview.explanation: Threshold wavelength λ₀ = hc / φ = (12400 eV·Å) / 4 eV = 3100 Å.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: Which electron configuration corresponds to a gas-phase oxygen atom in an excited state?
questionReview.mistakeHint: Your approach looks right but a computational slip derailed the answer. Double-check each arithmetic step and watch for sign/factor errors. Topic: Excited State Configurations.
questionReview.explanation: Oxygen (Z = 8) has 8 electrons. The ground state is 1s² 2s² 2p⁴. Promoting one 2s electron to the 2p orbital gives 1s² 2s¹ 2p⁵, which has 8 electrons in an excited configuration.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: If the kinetic energy of a particle is doubled, its de Broglie wavelength becomes:
questionReview.explanation: λ = h / √(2mE). If kinetic energy is doubled (E' = 2E), λ' = h / √(2m(2E)) = λ / √2 = (1/√2) times.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: The outermost electronic configuration of the most electronegative element is:
questionReview.explanation: Fluorine is the most electronegative element of all, belonging to group 17 (halogens) with valence configuration ns² np⁵.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: An electron has spin quantum number s = +1/2 and magnetic quantum number m = +2. It cannot be present in:
questionReview.explanation: The magnetic quantum number obeys −l ≤m ≤+l, so m = +2 requires l ≥2 (d or f orbital). Therefore, the electron cannot be present in an s-orbital (nor in a p-orbital). Recorded key: (a) s-orbital.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: Which one among the following statements is correct?
questionReview.explanation: l = 0 denotes an s-orbital (specifically 2s here), which is spherically symmetric. Statement (A) is correct.

options.text: An orbital containing an electron having quantum numbers n = 2, l = 0, m = 0 and s = +1/2 is spherical.
The frequency of X-rays is less than that of radio-waves.
As intensity of light increases, its frequency also increases.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: Correct order of radius of the 1st orbit of H, He⁺, Li²⁺, Be³⁺ is: [Given : Atomic No. H = 1, He = 2, Li = 3, Be = 4]
questionReview.explanation: Radius of n-th Bohr orbit is r_n = r₀ (n² / Z). For the 1st orbit (n = 1), r ∝1/Z. Since Z increases from H(1) to Be(4), radius decreases: H > He⁺ > Li²⁺ > Be³⁺.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: Which statement regarding the relative energies of monochromatic light with λ = 800 nm and monochromatic light with λ = 400 nm is correct?
questionReview.explanation: Energy per mole of photons is E = N_A (hc / λ). Since energy is inversely proportional to wavelength, 800 nm light has half the energy per mole as 400 nm light.

options.text: 800 nm light has half as much energy per mole of photons as 400 nm light
800 nm light has same energy per mole of photons as 400 nm light
800 nm light has twice as much energy per mole of photons as 400 nm light
No conclusion may be drawn regarding the relative energy per mole of photons without knowing the intensity of the light

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: Atoms of which element release the most energy when an electron is added to them in the gas phase?
questionReview.mistakeHint: The numerical approach is likely correct but the unit or scale used in the final step is off. Verify unit conversions and dimensional consistency.
questionReview.explanation: Sulfur has a more negative electron gain enthalpy (-200 kJ/mol) than oxygen (-141 kJ/mol) due to the smaller size and compact 2p subshell of oxygen leading to high electron-electron repulsions.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: The correct radial probability distribution curve for the hydrogen atomic orbital with principal quantum number n = 3 and azimuthal quantum number l = 1 is: (4π r² ψ² = radial probability density function and r = radial distance from the nucleus)
questionReview.explanation: For n = 3, l = 1 (a 3p orbital), the number of radial nodes is n −l −1 = 3 −1 −1 = 1. The radial probability distribution curve 4πr²ψ² therefore has two maxima separated by one node, with the outer maximum much taller than the inner maximum, corresponding to Graph (B).

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: How many orbitals are in an f sublevel (l = 3)?
questionReview.explanation: Number of orbitals in a subshell = 2l + 1. For l = 3 (f subshell), 2(3) + 1 = 7 orbitals.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: An element with atomic number 20 will be placed in which period of the periodic table?
questionReview.explanation: Z = 20 (Ca): 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁶4s² = [Ar]4s². The highest principal quantum number occupied is n = 4 (4th period).

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: The calculated value of spin only magnetic moment of ₂₆Fe³⁺ is:
questionReview.explanation: Fe³⁺ (Z = 26) has configuration [Ar]3d⁵ with n = 5 unpaired electrons. Spin-only magnetic moment μ = √(n(n+2)) = √(5 × 7) = √35 ≈5.92 BM.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: The ratio of (E₂ - E₁) to (E₄ - E₃) for the hydrogen atom is approximately equal to:

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: How many electrons will have m (magnetic quantum number) = 0 in ₂₆Fe³⁺ ion?
questionReview.explanation: ₂₆Fe³⁺ has 23 electrons: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁵. Each s subshell has 2 electrons with m = 0, each p subshell has 2 electrons with m = 0, and 3d⁵ has 1 electron with m = 0: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 11 (or 5 in the 3s, 3p, 3d shells).

questionReview.subject: Mathematics
questionReview.text: The exact numerical value of the expression tan²(π/16) + tan²(3π/16) + tan²(5π/16) + tan²(7π/16) is:
questionReview.explanation: Since tan(7π/16) = cot(π/16) and tan(5π/16) = cot(3π/16), the sum = [tan²A + cot²A] + [tan²B + cot²B] with A = π/16, B = 3π/16. tan²θ + cot²θ = (tanθ + cotθ)² −2 = 4/sin²2θ −2. So sum = 4/sin²(π/8) + 4/sin²(3π/8) −4. With sin²(π/8) = (2 −√2)/4 and sin²(3π/8) = (2 + √2)/4: 16/(2 −√2) + 16/(2 + √2) = 16·4/(4 −2) = 32. Sum = 32 −4 = 28.

questionReview.subject: Mathematics
questionReview.text: Find the sum of all real values of x satisfying the equation (x² − 5x + 5)^(x² + 4x − 60) = 1.
questionReview.explanation: Case 1: Base = 1 => x² - 5x + 5 = 1 => x² - 5x + 4 = 0 => x = 1, 4. Case 2: Exponent = 0 with base ≠0 => x² + 4x - 60 = 0 => (x+10)(x-6)=0 => x = -10, 6. Base at -10 is 155 ≠0, base at 6 is 11 ≠0. Case 3: Base = -1 with even exponent => x² - 5x + 5 = -1 => x² - 5x + 6 = 0 => x = 2, 3. For x=2, exp = 4+8-60 = -48 (even, valid). For x=3, exp = 9+12-60 = -39 (odd, rejected). Valid roots: 1, 4, -10, 6, 2. Sum = 1 + 4 - 10 + 6 + 2 = 3.

questionReview.subject: Mathematics
questionReview.text: Let z₁, z₂, z₃ be complex numbers such that |z₁| = 1, |z₂| = 2, and |z₃| = 3. If |z₁ + z₂ + z₃| = 1, the value of |9 z₁ z₂ + 4 z₁ z₃ + z₂ z₃| is:
questionReview.mistakeHint: Your approach looks right but a computational slip derailed the answer. Double-check each arithmetic step and watch for sign/factor errors. Topic: Modulus Properties.
questionReview.explanation: Note that |z₁|² = z₁ z̄₁ = 1 => 1/z₁ = z̄₁. Similarly, |z₂|² = 4 => 4/z₂ = z̄₂, and |z₃|² = 9 => 9/z₃ = z̄₃. Now, |9 z₁ z₂ + 4 z₁ z₃ + z₂ z₃| = |z₁ z₂ z₃| |9/z₃ + 4/z₂ + 1/z₁| = (1 × 2 × 3) |z̄₃ + z̄₂ + z̄₁| = 6 |z₁ + z₂ + z₃| = 6 × 1 = 6.

questionReview.subject: Mathematics
questionReview.text: The maximum value of |z| when z satisfies the condition |z - 4/z| = 2 is:
questionReview.explanation: By the triangle inequality: |z| = |(z - 4/z) + 4/z| ≤|z - 4/z| + 4/|z| = 2 + 4/|z|. Let r = |z|. Then r ≤2 + 4/r => r² - 2r - 4 ≤0 => r ≤(2 + √(4 + 16)) / 2 = 1 + √5. Therefore, max |z| = √5 + 1.

questionReview.subject: Mathematics
questionReview.text: If S_n = Σ(r = 1 to n) r/(r⁴ + r² + 1), then lim(n→∞) S_n is equal to:
questionReview.explanation: r⁴ + r² + 1 = (r² + r + 1)(r² - r + 1). The numerator r = 1/2 [(r² + r + 1) - (r² - r + 1)]. Thus the term is 1/2 [1/(r² - r + 1) - 1/(r² + r + 1)]. Telescoping sum gives 1/2 [1 - 1/(n² + n + 1)]. As n → ∞, the limit is 1/2.

questionReview.subject: Mathematics
questionReview.text: The number of integral values of x satisfying the system of inequalities x² - 10x - 11 ≤0 and x² - x - 2 > 0 is:
questionReview.explanation: First inequality: (x - 11)(x + 1) ≤0 => -1 ≤x ≤11. Second inequality: (x - 2)(x + 1) > 0 => x < -1 or x > 2. Intersection: x ∈(2, 11]. The integer values are 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 (9 values).

questionReview.subject: Mathematics
questionReview.text: Let α, β be the roots of x² − x − 1 = 0. Let P_n = α^n + β^n. Which of the following is true?
questionReview.explanation: Since α and β satisfy x² = x + 1, multiplying by x^(n−1) gives x^(n+1) = x^n + x^(n−1). Applying this to α and β and adding yields P_(n+1) = P_n + P_(n−1).

questionReview.subject: Mathematics
questionReview.text: The value of cos(2π/7) + cos(4π/7) + cos(6π/7) is:
questionReview.mistakeHint: Your approach looks right but a computational slip derailed the answer. Double-check each arithmetic step and watch for sign/factor errors. Topic: Cosine Series.
questionReview.explanation: Multiply and divide by 2 sin(π/7): 2 sin(π/7) [cos(2π/7) + cos(4π/7) + cos(6π/7)] = [sin(3π/7) - sin(π/7)] + [sin(5π/7) - sin(3π/7)] + [sin(7π/7) - sin(5π/7)] = sin(π) - sin(π/7) = -sin(π/7). Dividing by 2 sin(π/7) gives -1/2.

questionReview.subject: Mathematics
questionReview.text: If z = e^(iθ) (z ≠ −1), then (z − 1)/(z + 1) is always:
questionReview.mistakeHint: The reasoning started correctly but stopped short of the final answer. Multi-step problems need each intermediate result verified before moving on.
questionReview.explanation: (e^(iθ) − 1)/(e^(iθ) + 1) = [e^(iθ/2)(e^(iθ/2) − e^(−iθ/2))]/[e^(iθ/2)(e^(iθ/2) + e^(−iθ/2))] = 2i sin(θ/2)/(2 cos(θ/2)) = i tan(θ/2), which is purely imaginary.

questionReview.subject: Mathematics
questionReview.text: The set of all real x for which log_(0.5)(x² − 5x + 6) > −1 is:
questionReview.mistakeHint: The wrong formula or relationship was applied here. Revisit the relevant formulas for this topic and verify which one fits this scenario. Topic: Logarithmic Inequalities.
questionReview.explanation: Since the base 0.5 < 1, reversing the inequality gives x² - 5x + 6 < (0.5)⁻¹ = 2, and domain requires x² - 5x + 6 > 0. From x² - 5x + 6 < 2 => x² - 5x + 4 < 0 => (x - 1)(x - 4) < 0 => x ∈(1, 4). From domain: (x - 2)(x - 3) > 0 => x < 2 or x > 3. Intersection: x ∈(1, 2) ∪(3, 4).

questionReview.subject: Mathematics
questionReview.text: The total number of subsets of a finite set A having n elements is 56 more than the total number of subsets of another finite set B having m elements. The value of n² + m² is:
questionReview.explanation: Number of subsets of a set with n elements is 2ⁿ. Given 2ⁿ −2ᵐ= 56 = 2⁶ −2³ ⇒n = 6, m = 3. Recorded answer key option: (b) 45.

questionReview.subject: Mathematics
questionReview.text: If the roots of the equation ax² + bx + c = 0 are of the form α / (α - 1) and (α + 1) / α, then the value of (a + b + c)² is:
questionReview.explanation: Let p = α/(α −1) and q = (α + 1)/α. Then 1 −p = −1/(α −1) and 1 −q = −1/α, so (1 −p)(1 −q) = 1/[α(α −1)]. Also p −q = [α² −(α² −1)]/[α(α −1)] = 1/[α(α −1)]. Hence (1 −p)(1 −q) = p − q. Now (1 −p)(1 −q) = 1 −(p + q) + pq = 1 + b/a + c/a = (a + b + c)/a, and (p −q)² = (p + q)² −4pq = (b² −4ac)/a². Squaring: (a + b + c)²/a² = (b² −4ac)/a² ⇒(a + b + c)² = b² −4ac.

questionReview.subject: Mathematics
questionReview.text: If a, b, c are positive real numbers in HP, then the equation ax² - bx + c = 0 has roots that are:
questionReview.mistakeHint: Your approach looks right but a computational slip derailed the answer. Double-check each arithmetic step and watch for sign/factor errors. Topic: Harmonic Progression.
questionReview.explanation: b is the HM of a and c: b = 2ac / (a + c). Discriminant D = b² - 4ac = 4a²c²/(a + c)² - 4ac = 4ac [ac/(a+c)² - 1]. Since (a + c)² > 4ac > ac for distinct positive numbers, [ac/(a+c)² - 1] < 0 => D < 0. Thus roots are imaginary.

questionReview.subject: Mathematics
questionReview.text: The number of solutions of the equation sin⁴ x + cos⁴ x = sin x cos x in [0, 2π] is:
questionReview.mistakeHint: Your approach looks right but a computational slip derailed the answer. Double-check each arithmetic step and watch for sign/factor errors. Topic: Trigonometric Equations.
questionReview.explanation: sin⁴ x + cos⁴ x = 1 - 2 sin² x cos² x = 1 - (1/2) sin²(2x). Also sin x cos x = (1/2) sin(2x). Let t = sin(2x) ∈[-1, 1]. Then 1 - t²/2 = t/2 => t² + t - 2 = 0 => (t + 2)(t - 1) = 0 => t = 1. So sin(2x) = 1 in [0, 2π] => 2x = π/2, 5π/2 => x = π/4, 5π/4 (2 solutions).

questionReview.subject: Mathematics
questionReview.text: If 1, z₁, z₂, …, z_(n−1) are the n-th roots of unity, then (1 − z₁)(1 − z₂)…(1 − z_(n−1)) equals:
questionReview.mistakeHint: Your approach looks right but a computational slip derailed the answer. Double-check each arithmetic step and watch for sign/factor errors. Topic: Roots of Unity.
questionReview.explanation: z^n − 1 = (z − 1)(z − z₁)(z − z₂)…(z − z_(n−1)). Dividing by (z − 1): z^(n−1) + z^(n−2) + … + z + 1 = (z − z₁)(z − z₂)…(z − z_(n−1)). Setting z = 1 yields 1 + 1 + … + 1 (n terms) = n.

questionReview.subject: Mathematics
questionReview.text: The coefficient of x^n in the expansion of 1/[(1 − x)(1 − 2x)] is:
questionReview.explanation: 1/[(1 − x)(1 − 2x)] = 2/(1 − 2x) − 1/(1 − x) = 2Σ(k = 0 to ∞)(2x)^k − Σ(k = 0 to ∞)x^k. Therefore, the coefficient of x^n is 2^(n+1) − 1.

questionReview.subject: Mathematics
questionReview.text: Let f(x) = x² - 2x cos θ + 1. The sum of all roots (real and complex) of the equation f(f(x)) = 0 is:
questionReview.explanation: Let roots of f(t) = 0 be t₁ and t₂. Then t₁ + t₂ = 2 cos θ. For f(f(x)) = 0, we have f(x) = t₁ and f(x) = t₂. The sum of roots of x² - 2x cos θ + (1 - t₁) = 0 is 2 cos θ, and of x² - 2x cos θ + (1 -t₂) = 0 is 2 cos θ. Total sum of all 4 roots = 2 cos θ + 2 cos θ = 4 cos θ.

questionReview.subject: Mathematics
questionReview.text: Let ω be a complex cube root of unity with ω ≠ 1. A fair die is thrown three times. If r₁, r₂, r₃ are the numbers obtained on the die, find the probability that ω^(r₁) + ω^(r₂) + ω^(r₃) = 0. (Multiply your final probability by 216 to get the integer answer).
questionReview.explanation: ω³ = 1 and 1 + ω + ω² = 0. ω^{r₁} + ω^{r₂} + ω^{r₃} = 0 iff r₁, r₂, r₃ fall in distinct residue classes mod 3 ({1,4}, {2,5}, {3,6}). Number of ordered triples = 3! × 2 × 2 × 2 = 48. P = 48/216 = 2/9 ⇒216P = 48.

questionReview.text: If the quadratic equation x² + 2(a + 1)x + 9a - 5 = 0 has exactly one root in the interval (0, ∞) and a is an integer, find the sum of all possible values of a.
questionReview.explanation: For f(x) = x² + 2(a+1)x + (9a −5) = 0, under the restricted textbook reading of one positive root and one negative root with discriminant condition, a = 10 (flagged defective/unbounded in general since 9a −5 < 0 holds for all integers a ≤0).

questionReview.text: A complex number z satisfies |z - 3 - 4i| ≤5. Find the maximum possible value of |z|².
questionReview.explanation: |z −(3 + 4i)| ≤5 is a closed disc of radius 5 centred at C = 3 + 4i with |C| = 5.
